angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 27,369,534 km at 148.59 pc = 2.46 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: distance 148.588 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.064), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 148.588 +/- 9.51 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7176 +/- 0.1706 mas (same row, RUWE 0.87), 39.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 39.341 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: radius 39.341 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 371.904 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.089) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 27,369,534 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4044 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: effective temperature 4044 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.041) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 90037: effective temperature 4044 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.041) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
